skill.name: convex-expert
skill.description: Guides Convex backend development across schemas, functions, indexes, validation, storage, authentication, scheduled jobs, HTTP endpoints, and components.
skill.summary: Build and review Convex backends using documented patterns and deployment checks.
skill.author: get-convex

security_audit.summary: Most detections are Markdown backticks around API names, not shell execution. The verification rule does execute project tools and can deploy code or rewrite local Convex configuration without explicit approval.

remediation.issue: The workflow can push code to a Convex deployment and create an anonymous deployment without explicit user approval.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation before any deployment, anonymous project creation, or change to .env.local.

remediation.issue: The npx verification commands may download or execute packages selected from the project environment.
remediation.suggestion: Use installed, version-pinned project binaries and request confirmation before installing missing packages.

content.value_statement: Convex backend code can fail from invalid schemas, imports, validators, or query patterns. This skill applies Convex-specific rules and verification steps.
actual_capabilities: Reviews Convex schemas, indexes, queries, mutations, actions, and HTTP endpoints.
Applies object-form functions with argument and return validators.
Recommends indexed queries and bounded result patterns.
Distinguishes public functions from internal backend functions.
Guides schema evolution, file storage, scheduled jobs, and external input handling.
Runs TypeScript and Convex deployment checks when execution is approved.
limitations: Requires an existing Convex project and access to relevant source files.
Cannot guarantee production correctness without tests and project-specific requirements.
Deployment checks may change cloud state and local environment configuration.
Guidance reflects the skill content and may not cover later Convex platform changes.

use_cases.title: Create a Convex Feature
use_cases.description: Design validated functions, indexes, and schema changes for a new application workflow.

use_cases.title: Review Backend Reliability
use_cases.description: Find unbounded reads, invalid imports, missing validators, and unsafe schema migrations.

use_cases.title: Resolve Deployment Errors
use_cases.description: Interpret validation, schema, import, and runtime errors from Convex development checks.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Convex Function
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain this Convex function and identify its arguments, return value, database access, and visibility: [function].
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of an existing function

prompt_templates.title: Design a Data Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Convex schema and indexes for [feature]. Include validators, relationships, query paths, and migration notes.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Convex Directory
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [files] for validators, imports, indexes, bounded reads, internal visibility, runtime separation, and safe schema evolution.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Production Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a staged Convex migration for [change]. Address compatibility, backfill, indexes, rollback, tests, and deployment approval.

output_examples.input: Review a message-list query that filters the whole table and returns every matching row.
output: Add a schema index for the conversation identifier.
Replace the full-table filter with an indexed query.
Paginate results and validate both arguments and returns.

output_examples.input: Plan adding a required status field to an existing populated table.
output_examples.output: Add the field as optional, deploy compatibility changes, backfill existing records, verify completion, then make the validator required.

output_examples.input: Review a public mutation used only by a scheduled backend task.
output_examples.output: Convert the mutation to an internal function and update the scheduled task reference. Keep public access only when a client requires it.

best_practices: Provide the schema, related functions, expected behavior, and current errors.
Review generated Convex guidance before changing backend files.
Require approval before commands that deploy code or modify environment files.
anti_patterns: Do not request production deployment without identifying the target and approval boundary.
Do not omit project-specific authorization and data access requirements.
Do not treat generated recommendations as a substitute for tests and migration validation.

faq.question: What Convex code can this skill review?
faq.answer: It covers schemas, indexes, queries, mutations, actions, HTTP endpoints, scheduled jobs, storage, authentication wiring, and components.

faq.question: Does it write Convex functions?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create object-form functions with argument and return validators using the project context.

faq.question: Can it improve query performance?
faq.answer: It identifies full-table scans, recommends indexes, and uses pagination or bounded reads where appropriate.

faq.question: Will it deploy changes automatically?
faq.answer: The source workflow requests deployment verification. Users should require explicit approval before any local or cloud state change.

faq.question: Does it support schema migrations?
faq.answer: It recommends staged changes, optional fields, backfills, and later validator tightening for populated tables.

faq.question: What context produces the best results?
faq.answer: Provide the current schema, related functions, generated guidance, requirements, errors, and deployment constraints.
